rows.scope: OCME 'mode of death' count: drowning cases the Maine OCME handled in the calendar year. All manners included ('These deaths may be accidents, suicides or homicides'), so NOT accidental-only and NOT an ICD-10 vital-statistics count. Boating (water transport) drownings are not separated and are presumably inside the count (the OCME takes all deaths not known to be exclusively natural); not stated. No split by water body or activity is printed. The report says a clear-cut drowning may carry cause 'drowning' with manner undetermined; whether such cases are in the count is not stated.
rows.geography: Maine (deaths under Office of Chief Medical Examiner jurisdiction; residency and place-of-death basis not stated)
rows.source: Maine Office of Chief Medical Examiner, 2025 Annual Report (Attorney General's Documents collection, Digital Maine, online 2026), section 'Categorizations of Modes of Death', bar chart of Firearm / Drowning / Child (<2 years) / Fire Related counts by year, p. 9

notes: Source found: the Maine Office of Chief Medical Examiner annual reports (2023, 2024, 2025 editions on Digital Maine, Attorney General's Documents) each print a bar chart of OCME 'modes of death' by year with a Drowning column. Values: 2020 43, 2021 29, 2022 31, 2023 31, 2024 26, 2025 37. Overlapping years agree across all editions. Definition: cases the OCME handled, all manners ('These deaths may be accidents, suicides or homicides'); not accidental-only; boating drownings not separated; no place/activity split printed anywhere in the reports. The reports do not say whether the counts are deaths occurring in Maine or Maine residents, nor whether undetermined-manner drownings are included. Values were read from the PDF text extraction of a chart, not from a table: a person with a browser should open the 2025 report (article=1033) p. 9 and confirm the drowning bars visually; the extracted Firearm value for 2025 (358, vs 192 in 2024) looks anomalous and is a reason to check the chart. Accidental-only pie chart: 'Breakdown of Accidental Deaths by Mode' lists Drowning at 2% (2023 and 2024 editions) and 3% (2025 edition) of OCME accidental deaths, label-value pairing inferred from order; not recorded as rows. Not found: a Maine CDC (death-certificate, ICD-10) count of unintentional drowning by year, and any official split by water body or activity (sea, river, lake, pool, boating). CDC WONDER (W65-W74 plus V90, V92, Maine, 2019-2024) and WISQARS need an interactive session and were not tried. USCG state tables (boating deaths by state and year) sit beyond the reachable part of the PDF. Press corroboration (Sun Journal, June 2021, citing the medical examiner's office): 43 in 2020, 32 in 2019, 34 in 2018.
